column6: Older text: Q3 says federal university research funding was "essentially zero" before 1940 (land-grant and agricultural experiment station funding existed).

Bullet 4 called air pressure a "quality you felt" before the barometer; air pressure was not a felt quality, it had no measure until Torricelli (1643). Older text: Explainer says Lippershey's telescope was patented (the patent was refused); Q5 says the LHC works on the cyclotron's principle (it is a synchrotron).

Bullet 3 called universities "relatively peripheral"; that older thesis is contested (Galileo, Newton, Vesalius, Harvey all studied or taught at universities). Hedged. Older text: Q3 makes the same claim; Core gives 1550-1750 while Explainer gives 1543-1700.
Older text: Q2 says lunar samples "revealed" the Moon formed by giant impact; they supported that hypothesis.

Bullet 2 attributed the explanation of fission to Meitner alone; it was Meitner and Otto Frisch (1939). Older text: Core says du Chatelet could publish only under her husband's name (she published under her own); Q1 calls Edmund Wilson Nettie Stevens's supervisor (her adviser was T. H. Morgan); Q3 has an encoding glitch "?mv2" for (1/2)mv^2.
